summary: BBN proposes redefining IMP-to-Host error message types and adding new ones so hosts can choose better recovery actions. It includes a new message for when the IMP dropped its ready line, and invites objections before the change.

eli5.summary: The network box wants to give clearer error messages to the computer, so the computer knows what to do.

questions: imp to host error messages proposal
imp to host error message types
subtitle: BBN proposes clearer IMP-to-Host error messages so Hosts can pick the right recovery action.

tldr.problem: IMP-to-Host error message types 1 and 8 did not tell Hosts enough to decide how to recover.
tldr.mechanism: The IMP would redefine types 1 and 8, add types 10, 11 and 12 for specific errors, and send a new type 13 message when it drops its Ready Line.
tldr.outcome: This is a proposal that asks for objections within a few months; the RFC does not report how it turned out.

today: The unit metadata lists this RFC's status as Unknown, and no RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it. The RFC is a proposal and does not say whether the changes were installed as described.

sections.title: The Proposed Change
sections.content:
Alex McKenzie of BBN announces that BBN is considering a redefinition of the IMP-to-Host error message types (type 1 and type 8) and the creation of additional error types. The goal is to help Hosts decide on an appropriate recovery action without causing serious reprogramming problems.

BBN plans to install the changes within a few months, so it asks to hear about any strong negative reactions relatively quickly.
sections.eli5: The people who run the network boxes say they want to change the error notes. They ask everyone to speak up soon if they dislike the idea.

sections.title: A General Error Message
sections.content:
When a Host has been unresponsive to queued input for a long time, the IMP drops its Ready Line for a short period. That sets the IMP's error flip-flops (see RFC 270). The IMP then sends the Host a few NOPs and resumes normal operation.

BBN proposes to also send a new message, type 13. It tells the Host that the Ready Line was dropped, that the error flop was set, and that the IMP will answer the next completed Host-to-IMP message with a type 1 or type 8 message.
sections.eli5: If the computer ignores the box for too long, the box rings a bell. The new note says, 'I rang the bell, so expect an error message next.'

sections.title: Errors for Specific Messages
sections.content:
Five error types answer specific Host-to-IMP transmissions. Where the message can be identified, the error carries its source and link number bits.

  • Type 1 is redefined: the error flip-flop was set on a message the IMP cannot identify.
  • Type 8 is redefined: the flip-flop was set during receipt of the message identified by the source and link number bits.
  • Type 10 is new: a Host-to-IMP message was too short and cannot be identified.
  • Type 11 is new: a message was too long; it is identified by source and link number.
  • Type 12 is new: a message had an illegal message type code; it is identified by source and link number, but the erroneous type code is not included.
sections.eli5: Instead of one vague 'something broke' note, the box would have separate notes for 'too short', 'too long' and 'I do not know that kind of message'.

items.label: Error, unidentified message
items.desc: Error flip-flop set on a message the IMP cannot identify (redefined).

items.label: Error, identified message
items.desc: Error flip-flop set during receipt of the identified message (redefined).

items.label: Too short
items.desc: Host-to-IMP message too short and cannot be identified (new).

items.label: Too long
items.desc: Host-to-IMP message too long; identified by source and link number (new).

items.label: Illegal type
items.desc: Illegal message type code; identified by source and link number (new).

items.label: General error
items.desc: Ready Line was dropped and error flop set (new).
